name: Judah
overview: Judah is a male member of the tribe of Levi, noted specifically as one of the Levites who returned with Zerubbabel. His unique mention in Nehemiah 12:8 highlights his role among the Levites during the post-exilic restoration period. Beyond this, no additional personal notes are recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Judah means 'praised,' reflecting a proper Hebrew name without indication of divine naming in this instance. This meaning aligns with the biblical tradition of names carrying significance, though here it is simply stated.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Judah as a descendant of Levi, establishing his lineage within the priestly tribe. No further family relationships are documented in the given references.
scriptureSignificance: Judah’s importance lies in his identification as a Levite who returned with Zerubbabel, contributing to the reestablishment of worship and community after the exile. This connection places him within the faithful remnant committed to restoring God’s covenant practices. His lineage, while distinct from the more famous Judah son of Jacob, still reflects the faithful service of the Levites in biblical history.
